title: Evaluation preserves K-injective complexes of inverse systems
statement: Evaluation preserves K-injective complexes of inverse systems. Let A be an abelian category, I a K-injective cochain complex in the functor category from the opposite natural-number poset to A [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], and n an object of that poset. The complex whose p-th object is (I.X p)(n), with evaluated differentials, is K-injective in A. No product-exactness, enough-injectives, boundedness or epimorphic-transition assumptions are required.

source.place: Tag 070M context; exact-adjoint argument from lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective, using Mathlib CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Evaluation and exact finite coproducts

proof.text: The Mathlib evaluation left adjoint sends X at m to the coproduct indexed by morphisms n to m. This hom type is subsingleton and therefore finite. The composite with evaluation at m is naturally isomorphic to the constant-diagram functor followed by its finite coproduct. Finite coproducts are exact in an abelian category, so this composite preserves finite limits. Finite limits in the tower category are computed pointwise. The left adjoint thus preserves finite limits; it preserves colimits by adjunction and is additive.
Apply the exact-left-adjoint criterion to the evaluation adjunction; the functor applied to I is definitionally I.asFunctor.obj n.
